Decide every pending change that matches a predicate. The call succeeds even when rows fail: the failed rows are printed after the decided ids, so compare them with what you intended. --reason is required for reject.

Post a comment on a change (1 to 4000 characters of plain text). --visibility is required and fixed once posted: everyone is read by everyone who can read the change, approvers_only by the people who can decide it. A comment is never a decision; there is no edit or delete. Needs a signed-in session.

Admins and auditors see every change; other members see only their own.

Read one page of events in order, after a known event or from a position in the audit log (warden.checkpoint events included). Prints the page: events, nextCursor, hasMore. Page on with --after-audit-event-id set to the last event while hasMore is true. Needs the audit log's access.

Follow the audit log live, one event per line, until interrupted (Ctrl-C). Repeat --type (or comma-separate) to keep only those event types. Each event has auditEventId, type, actorType, occurredAt and outcome, plus eventId (the stream frame's id); read the full row with query. Each event prints once. With --json (or --output json) each line is one JSON object. Needs the org-owner, org-admin, project-admin or project-auditor role; an extension cannot tail.

Rotate the active key: a new version is created, every data key is re-wrapped under it and the old version is revoked. Writes to the project's encrypted data wait while it runs. Needs project-admin, a person's sign-in and a fresh MFA step-up. Without --step-up-proof-cmd, a required step-up is printed (the challenge too) and the command exits non-zero; complete the step-up, then run it again. With --step-up-proof-cmd your command answers the challenge: it gets the challenge as JSON on stdin and the HTTP method and URL in K9O_STEPUP_METHOD and K9O_STEPUP_URL, and prints {"method":"dpop|mtls|webauthn","proof":"..."} on stdout. The request is then sent once more with the proof; nothing else is retried. At most 3 rotations in 24 hours.
